blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. Conventional early-exit decoding halts after initial passes without cache completion, truncating cached key-value states of past tokens to shallow depth. We study the opposite strategy, late entry, where new tokens skip initial passes and enter directly into the final K < T passes over a deep context cache. Once lightweight fine-tuning resolves hidden-state norm mismatch at the entry boundary, deep cached context substitutes for skipped token-local passes, allowing late entry to outperform matched early exit across model families and pass budgets. To turn this asymmetry into wall-clock speedups without stalling to build deep caches, candidate blocks verify through only the final K passes on the critical path while previously committed tokens complete passes 1 -> T alongside subsequent steps at zero extra serial calls. Projecting these finished T-pass wake states inside the existing output GEMM (Wake verification, governed by logit-margin tolerance tau in [0, inf]) unifies greedy-exact T-pass decoding (tau = 0, matching K = T block decoding within bf16 reduction order), margin-gated verification (tau > 0), and non-rollback lossy late entry (tau = inf) inside a single static CUDA graph. On Ouro-2.6B (T = 4), K = 2 Wake reaches 5.2x greedy-exact speedup at tau = 0 (+26% over K = 4 block decoding on GSM8K) and 6.8x at tau = inf (+16.9 points over trained early exit at matched speed). Scaling test-time recurrence across T in {8, 16, 32, 64} on Huginn-3.5B cuts K = T/4 rollbacks 21.5x with depth, driving greedy-exact (tau = 0) speedups to 6.1x (T = 32) and 8.4x (T = 64, +153% over K = 64 block) and tau = inf speedups to 10.6 to 12.5x.

1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Looped language models scale test-time compute without increasing model size by passing
each token repeatedly through a shared Transformer stack for T T recurrent passes ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Geiping et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) . During autoregressive
decoding, however, running all T T passes per generated token turns recurrence depth
directly into sequential latency. When each new token is restricted to K < T K<T serial
passes, which passes should it execute? As shown in Figure 1 ,
conventional early exit without cache completion ( Schuster et al., 2022 ) runs
the first K K passes and halts (Figure 1 b), leaving past key-value (KV)
caches truncated at shallow depth K K so all future tokens attend to immature context
states. We explore the opposite choice, late entry , which skips initial passes
and feeds each new token’s embedding directly into the final K K passes over a deep
context KV cache (Figure 1 c).

blocks.en:
At first glance, skipping initial passes seems destined to fail: on off-the-shelf
Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B ( T = 4 T=4 ) ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) , feeding raw embeddings into a late
pass breaks predictions immediately because late passes expect normalized hidden states
from earlier passes. Once lightweight fine-tuning aligns late passes to accept raw
embeddings, however, a clear asymmetry emerges between token depth and context depth:
one final pass over a four-pass context matches full-depth predictions more closely than
two initial passes over a two-pass context ( + 10 + +10+ accuracy points in sequential
decoding). Under identical training data, hyperparameters, and steps, spending K K serial passes at the end of the recurrence consistently outperforms spending them at the
beginning across both Ouro scales ( T = 4 T=4 ; Section 2 ) and 32 32 -pass
middle-recurrent Huginn-3.5B ( T = 32 T=32 ; Section 4.4 ), showing that deep
cached context retains much of the benefit of recurrent depth.

embeddings ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) . For clarity, Sections 2 and 3 develop our analysis and pipeline on T = 4 T=4 Ouro before
Section 4.4 scales both to 32 32 -pass middle-recurrent Huginn-3.5B
( T = 32 T=32 ).

In free autoregressive generation, a single altered prediction changes every
subsequent token, confounding single-step accuracy with trajectory drift. To measure
per-token prediction quality cleanly, we first evaluate teacher-forced
agreement (Appendix A ). We generate reference completions greedily at
full depth ( T = 4 T=4 ), replay the exact same token prefixes under a reduced-pass
configuration, and record the fraction of positions whose greedy next-token
prediction matches full depth.

blocks.en: 3 Late-Entry Decoding
blocks.zh: 3 晚进解码

blocks.en:
While Section 2 assumed idealized full-depth context states, a
practical decoder must construct those states for newly generated tokens without
stalling generation. Late-entry decoding achieves this by maintaining deep context
with a short pipeline lag across decoding steps. For a concrete mental model at T = 4 T=4 and K = 2 K=2 (previewed in Figure 5 ), each decoding step performs
three coordinated actions: 1. Tentative late-pass verification: new candidate tokens skip passes 1 1 and 2 2 and execute only passes 3 3 and 4 4 ( K = 2 K=2 serial calls) to emit a tentatively accepted token group. 2. Provisional KV exposure: newly accepted tokens temporarily populate
slots 3 3 and 4 4 with provisional KV states computed from their embeddings so
the next step can proceed immediately without stalling. 3. Pipelined cache completion and Wake verification: over the next two
decoding steps, those tentative tokens ride along inside ongoing forward calls to
compute true passes 1 → 2 1\to 2 and 3 → 4 3\to 4 at zero extra serial calls ,
overwriting provisional KV entries and verifying finished T T -pass states inside the
same output GEMM to advance a permanently verified T T -pass prefix. We formalize looped pass mechanics in Section 3.1 , describe
within-step block verification in Section 3.2 , detail cross-step
cache completion in Section 3.3 , and unify greedy-exact and lossy decoding
via Wake verification in Section 3.4 (hardware Roofline and concurrency
scaling follow in Section 4.7 ).

blocks.en:
Looped and recursive language models iterate a weight-tied layer stack to scale latent
reasoning depth at a compact parameter footprint ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Bae et al., 2025a ; Bae et al., 2025b ; Geiping et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) .
In standard non-recurrent Transformers, SkipDecode ( Del Corro et al., 2023 ) skips bottom layers in favor of upper layers under a monotonically decreasing per-step
layer budget so KV caches never require recomputation, while in shared-weight recursive
models Relaxed Recursive Transformers ( Bae et al., 2025a ) introduce cross-request
depth-wise batching and Mixture-of-Recursions ( Bae et al., 2025b ) learns token-level
routing across initial passes. Our analysis addresses a distinct regime: because a
looped model shares weights across all passes, every token can enter uniformly at the
final K K passes without decaying position budgets, while within-sequence pipelined
cache completion reconstructs exact 1 → T 1\to T context caches in the background wake.

To accelerate autoregressive decoding, speculative and block-decoding methods verify
multiple drafted tokens in parallel using auxiliary drafters, n-gram suffix lookups,
or single-pass mask placeholders ( Leviathan et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2023 ; Cai et al., 2024 ; Fu et al., 2024 ; Gloeckle et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2026a ; Jin et al., 2026 ) .
For looped language models specifically, WaveFront ( Ha and Kim, 2026 ) , LoopSpec ( Cho et al., 2026 ) , DAS ( Li et al., 2026 ) , and LoopAhead ( Liu et al., 2026c ) accelerate drafting via shallow initial passes: DAS and LoopAhead verify
candidates synchronously through a full T T -pass target call, whereas WaveFront and
LoopSpec pipeline single-pass shallow guesses diagonally into deeper passes.
Crucially, because those methods only speed up proposal generation while still routing
every accepted token through shallow-to-deep passes on the verification path, full T T -pass verification bounds their speedup as recurrence deepens. Late entry paired with
Wake verification is complementary and structurally distinct along three axes:
(1) our optimistic frontier executes the final K < T K<T passes over a deep context
